notes:
Summary: POC for customer support + product reranking. Took 8 weeks from discovery -> eval. Heavily price-sensitive retail POC. Final decision: chose OpenAI direct API (simple pricing + brand comfort).

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-11-06: Intro call (Sofia) — customer interested in reducing call-center deflection and improving search conversion.
- 2025-11-20: Technical scoping with Marcus (SE). Discussed latency targets (95th < 200ms) and regional residency CA/US.
- 2025-12-10: POC kickoff — sample dataset for embeddings + chat flow. Fireflies: ff_2026-01-18_maplewood_poc-demo.
- 2026-01-18: Demo + results: embeddings recall improved but cost per 1M tokens higher than internal threshold.
- 2026-01-25: Security questionnaire submitted (Maplewood security team). They flagged requirement for strict vendor SSO + SOC2 + residency; asked about KMS/HSM for private deployments.
- 2026-01-30: Pricing review call — customer said "we need something plug-and-play, minimal ops; legal prefers known brands."
- 2026-02-12: Final procurement review. Finance paused spend due to FY26 budget freeze; procurement recommended direct vendor (OpenAI) to simplify contract.
- 2026-02-20: Internal decision: choose OpenAI direct API. Sales notified; deal marked closed-lost.

Customer quotes / color:
- "We need predictable SLAs but can't staff more infra ops right now." — Head of ML
- Procurement: "Simpler contract and market familiarity wins for us; less integration risk."

Technical / business requirements captured:
- Workloads: chat for CS (low latency), embeddings for search and product rerank.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 200ms for chat. Throughput peak: ~120 rps for reranking during promo spikes.
- Cost sensitivity: target < $X per 1M tokens (negotiated internally).
- Security: SOC2 mandatory, SSO/SAML, audit logs, ability to route EU traffic to EU region. KMS integration desired but not blocker.
- Ops preference: minimal integration effort, managed endpoint, clear pricing.

Why lost / lessons learned:
- Primary factor: brand and simplicity — procurement explicitly wanted a large, familiar vendor (OpenAI) to reduce perceived integration risk.
- Secondary: budget freeze pushed them to choose a vendor with simpler procurement path.
- Tertiary: internal champion left the project mid-POC; momentum slowed.
- Opportunity: customer liked Redwood performance and caching plan; price negotiations got close but timing/budget terminated the deal.

Next actions (internal):
- Document negotiation points and pricing gap; add to lost-reasons board.
- Share security answers used in POC with GTM to refine enterprise FAQ (KMS, residency specifics).
- Re-engage Q3 FY26 after budget refresh — target exec sponsor (Head of Product/Head of Ops).

Misc references:
- Pricing deck: /drive/decks/Maplewood_Redwood_Pricing_Deck_v3.pdf
- Security QA: /drive/security/Maplewood_Security_QA_2026-01.md
- Jira follow-up (SUP-1129) for KMS integration question.

Status: Closed-lost to OpenAI direct API. Marked for re-engage in Q3 if budget and champion return.
